svg.text: index.ts imports MonitoringService, which imports clientFactory.ts for the first time in the process.
const restClient = new RestDeviceClient(); // clientFactory.ts, line 5
Runs at 14:37:36.631Z — 0.3 seconds before "rest service started" even logs. No request has arrived yet.
Node caches the finished module. Every later "import { discoverProtocol } from './clientFactory'" —
from monitoringService.ts or anywhere else — reuses this same restClient, never rebuilds it.
PHASE 2 — 14:37:38.319Z, 1.4 seconds later — a real curl -X POST /devices arrives
MonitoringService.registerDevice({ name: "router-1", address: "localhost:4001" }) runs, and calls:
discoverProtocol lives in clientFactory.ts and reads "restClient" — a variable declared ABOVE it in the
SAME file. Ordinary JavaScript closure/scope, not dependency injection: any function can see any variable
declared earlier in its own module, the same way it can see an imported name.
restClient already existed — built 1.4s earlier in Phase 1. Result: protocol:"rest", the real router's capabilities.
Register switch-1, camera-rest-1, etc. and Phase 2 repeats for each — Phase 1 still never runs again.
Real timestamps from an actual run of your project, 2026-09-09 — not simulated.
